judge_reasoning: The model presents a rules-legal variation of the official line. Waiting until after blockers to sacrifice both Sacred Cats ensures Vampire Cutthroat is unavoidably unblocked due to skulk, then makes both Vampires 3/3. Regardless of whether or how Indulgent Aristocrat is blocked, the two Vampires deal 6 total damage and gain 6 life through lifelink. Sacrificing the 3/3 Cutthroat then reaches 30 life, enabling Ayli's second ability after embalming a Cat. The mana costs total exactly ten with sufficient colored sources. Exiling Gideon disables the emblem while the opponent is at 0 or less life, causing them to lose.
model_solution:
1. Precombat main: cast Sacred Cat from hand ({W}). Do not play anything else. (Mana used: 1.)
2. Attack with Vampire Cutthroat and Indulgent Aristocrat only. Keep Ayli and both Sacred Cats home. Cutthroat has skulk. All of the opponent's creatures have power 3 or more, so none can block it. The opponent may or may not block Aristocrat.
3. After blockers are declared, activate Indulgent Aristocrat ({2}, sacrifice Sacred Cat #1). Each Vampire gets a +1/+1 counter. Activate it again ({2}, sacrifice Sacred Cat #2). Cutthroat and Aristocrat are now both 3/3. (Mana used: 4, total 5.)
4. Combat damage: Cutthroat deals 3 to the opponent, taking them to 0, but the Gideon emblem stops them losing. Aristocrat deals 3 to its blocker, or to the opponent if unblocked. Both have lifelink, so life goes from 21 to 27.
5. Second main phase: activate Ayli's first ability ({1}), sacrificing Vampire Cutthroat. You gain 3 life, its toughness, and go to 30. (Total mana 6.)
6. Activate Embalm on a Sacred Cat card in the graveyard ({W}) to make a token Sacred Cat. (Total mana 7.)
7. Activate Ayli's second ability ({1}{W}{B}), sacrificing the token Cat. You have 30 life, which is 10 more than the starting 20, so it is legal. Target Gideon of the Trials; it is exiled. (Total mana 10.)
8. The opponent no longer controls a Gideon planeswalker, so the emblem stops protecting them. They are at 0 or less life and lose as a state-based action.

Puzzle conventions:
Winning
Unless otherwise stated, you must win the puzzle by inflicting lethal damage to your opponent before the turn ends. This can be as late as during the cleanup step if necessary. Your solution must work for all possible outcomes, such as your opponent’s actions and blocking decisions (see below.)
Phase
Unless otherwise stated, you begin each puzzle at the beginning of your first main phase. You have already drawn a card and gone past upkeep triggers. You have not yet played a land, cast any spells, activated any abilities of permanents on the battlefield, or attacked.
Your Opponent’s Resources / Actions
Unless otherwise stated, your opponent has no cards in hand and no other permanents in play (including no lands – despite the lack of realism there.) This means the only actions you need to consider are activated abilities with no mana cost. Most puzzles with opponent actions will offer more information on this.
Blocking
You cannot assume that your opponent will block a certain way, unless they are somehow forced to. Your solution must satisfy all possible blocking scenarios, even ones that would seem strange in a regular game, and always deal lethal in order to be correct.
Dice
Sometimes you will see six-sided dice placed on cards. These are meant to indicate counters, of whatever type is most reasonable to be there. On most creatures they will be +1/+1 counters, on most artifacts and lands they will be charge counters, and on most Planeswalkers they will be loyalty counters.
If the card specifies a type of counter itself, however (like Icatian Javelineers or Raging Ravine), that will dictate which type it is. 
For -1/-1 counters, we will use a separate graphic to avoid confusion.
Zones
Unless otherwise stated, all zones not displayed are empty. Neither you nor your opponent have cards in graveyards or in exile.
Cards Drawn from Libraries
In any puzzle in which either player might draw cards or otherwise access their library, the puzzle will stipulate some known or assumed information about the library.
Most commonly, this will be a statement that you should assume that the cards remaining in libraries are to be assumed to be irrelevant to the puzzle.
Your Life
Occasionally, your own life total might appear to matter – for cards like Anguished Unmaking, for example. If we require you to consider your own life total in a puzzle, it will be displayed.
If your life total is not shown, you may assume it is irrelevant and effectively infinite.

When you are ready to answer, put your final winning line inside <solution> tags:

<solution>
1. First step...
2. Second step...
</solution>

Your line must be legal under the rules and must win against all possible opponent responses and blocking decisions.

Opponent is at 3 life, but Gideon's emblem means they can't lose while they control a Gideon planeswalker. So the plan has three parts. First, put them to 0 or less in combat. Second, reach 30 life, which Ayli's exile ability requires (10 more than the starting 20). Third, exile Gideon with Ayli, after which the opponent loses to state-based actions.

Ayli's damage is prevented, so she stays home as the engine. I checked the mana and life totals: 10 lands cover every cost, and life reaches exactly 30.

<solution>
1. Precombat main: cast Sacred Cat from hand ({W}). Do not play anything else. (Mana used: 1.)
2. Attack with Vampire Cutthroat and Indulgent Aristocrat only. Keep Ayli and both Sacred Cats home. Cutthroat has skulk. All of the opponent's creatures have power 3 or more, so none can block it. The opponent may or may not block Aristocrat.
3. After blockers are declared, activate Indulgent Aristocrat ({2}, sacrifice Sacred Cat #1). Each Vampire gets a +1/+1 counter. Activate it again ({2}, sacrifice Sacred Cat #2). Cutthroat and Aristocrat are now both 3/3. (Mana used: 4, total 5.)
4. Combat damage: Cutthroat deals 3 to the opponent, taking them to 0, but the Gideon emblem stops them losing. Aristocrat deals 3 to its blocker, or to the opponent if unblocked. Both have lifelink, so life goes from 21 to 27.
5. Second main phase: activate Ayli's first ability ({1}), sacrificing Vampire Cutthroat. You gain 3 life, its toughness, and go to 30. (Total mana 6.)
6. Activate Embalm on a Sacred Cat card in the graveyard ({W}) to make a token Sacred Cat. (Total mana 7.)
7. Activate Ayli's second ability ({1}{W}{B}), sacrificing the token Cat. You have 30 life, which is 10 more than the starting 20, so it is legal. Target Gideon of the Trials; it is exiled. (Total mana 10.)
8. The opponent no longer controls a Gideon planeswalker, so the emblem stops protecting them. They are at 0 or less life and lose as a state-based action.
</solution>
